name: Mithras

attributes.attribute: a Persian deity imported into Celtic lands by the Roman legions
worshipped in Britain around Hadrian's Wall
honored in Mithraea with the blood rite of the Taurobolium

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Mithras was a Persian deity who spread into Celtic lands. He was most worshipped in Britain around the region of Hadrian's Wall. Mithras was not a Celtic god but was imported by the Roman legions. Many legionnaires held a special devotion to him. His temples, called Mithraea, were the site of a blood rite called the Taurobolium. In this rite a worshiper was drenched in the blood of a newly slaughtered bull as a kind of baptism. There is no evidence that the Celts used the rite. They had their own bull ritual, the bull-sleep.
objective: Document the Persian god Mithras in the Celtic world.
